title: Trailing/profit-protecting stop ('Don't Let a Winning Trade Turn into a Loss', ch. 54)
description: Ch. 54 has a whole subsection, 'Don't Let a Winning Trade Turn into a Loss,' not implemented at all today: as unrealized profit grows, move the stop to breakeven ('cuffing the trade') once profit crosses some threshold, then keep ratcheting the stop up to protect a growing fraction of open profit as it increases (Elder's own example: a third). This is a distinct, new feature from the existing static SafeZone protective_stop -- a trailing/profit-protecting stop that reacts to how far a position has moved in its favor, not just current volatility. Must enforce the companion principle 'Move Your Stop Only in the Direction of Your Trade': a stop is never loosened once set, only tightened -- implement as a hard ratchet, not a fresh computation each time.

checklist.step: Design and implement a trailing/profit-protecting stop function taking a position's entry price, current price, and existing SafeZone stop, returning a ratcheted stop for a long position.

Decide and record (a decisions entry) the exact breakeven-trigger threshold and profit-protection fraction -- Elder's own numbers are illustrative examples, not stated hard rules, so this needs an explicit, documented judgment call.
Enforce the ratchet as max(previous suggested stop, newly computed stop) for a long -- never let the returned stop decrease across successive calls.

Unit tests: profit below threshold (no change from SafeZone), profit crossing threshold (moves to breakeven), profit growing further (ratchets up), and a test proving the stop never decreases across a sequence of calls even if a later computed value would be lower.
Wire the new trailing stop into GET /api/portfolio/risk alongside the existing protective_stop field, without breaking existing consumers of that field.
elder-signal-reviewer pass before merge (this is signal/risk logic).

decisions.decision: Breakeven-trigger threshold = 10% unrealized profit (as a fraction of entry price); profit-protection fraction = 1/3 (Elder's own worked example, reused verbatim) applied to profit EARNED BEYOND that 10% trigger, not to total profit. app.portfolio.risk.trailing_profit_stop(entry_price, current_price, safezone_stop): below the trigger, returns safezone_stop verbatim (unchanged from the existing static SafeZone behavior -- there's no 'winning trade' yet to protect); at or above it, returns entry_price + (1/3 * profit_beyond_threshold), which is exactly entry_price (breakeven) the instant the trigger first fires and rises continuously beyond that.
decisions.rationale: Elder states the ch. 54 'Don't Let a Winning Trade Turn into a Loss' behavior (move to breakeven once profit has grown enough, then keep protecting a growing fraction of profit) but gives no stated hard number for either the trigger or general applicability of 'a third' -- both are explicit judgment calls, as the checklist itself flags. 10% was chosen as large enough that ordinary daily noise on this app's swing/position timeframe won't false-trigger it long before a real trend move has developed, small enough that a genuinely winning trade isn't left unprotected for long; a fixed dollar/point amount was rejected as not scaling across tickers of very different price levels, and a threshold defined as a multiple of the position's own stop-distance ('1R') was rejected as needing that stop-distance to be tracked at entry time, which this app doesn't persist anywhere today. 1/3 is reused directly from the book's own example rather than picked independently, since it's the one concrete number the text actually gives. Applying the fraction to profit BEYOND the trigger (not total profit) was chosen over the simpler 'entry_price + fraction * total_profit' alternative specifically because the latter would already sit above breakeven at the moment of crossing (a discontinuity), contradicting the book's own framing of that moment as landing exactly on breakeven ('cuffing the trade').

decisions.decision: The hard ratchet (never decrease across successive real GET /api/portfolio/risk calls) is implemented as a stateless recomputation over the position's own full price history since entry (app.portfolio.risk.ratchet_trailing_profit_stop), not as a persisted database column mutated on each read. Once the breakeven trigger has fired at least once, the returned value is the running max of entry_price + fraction*profit_beyond_threshold across every close from position.entry_date through today, folded fresh on every call; the live, independently-fluctuating safezone_stop participates only as a pre-trigger pass-through and is deliberately never re-folded into the ratchet once triggered.
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected: adding a nullable `trailing_stop` column to PositionORM (mirroring the entry_notes/strategy precedent) and mutating it inside GET /api/portfolio/risk's handler on every read, taking max(persisted_value, freshly_computed_candidate) and writing the result back. Rejected for three reasons: (1) it would be this codebase's first GET endpoint with a side-effecting write, a genuine architectural deviation from every other route here; (2) POST /api/portfolio/positions's same-ticker merge can change avg_cost_basis/entry_date after a trailing_stop was already persisted against the OLD cost basis, and correctly re-basing a persisted ratchet across that merge would need its own invalidation logic this task would otherwise have to design and test; (3) app.data.base.DataProvider.get_daily_ohlcv already fetches this ticker's full available history (not a truncated window), so every caller in this endpoint already has everything the stateless approach needs in hand at zero extra fetch cost. The stateless fold is mathematically safe against ever decreasing across successive calls for exactly the reason a persisted ratchet would be: daily OHLCV bars only ever accumulate over real time, never get revised away once committed to history, so a later call's fold is always over a superset of an earlier call's -- the running max over a growing set can only hold steady or rise. The one deliberate accepted trade-off: safezone_stop is NOT re-folded into the ratchet post-trigger (using today's single live safezone_stop value for every historical day, rather than reconstructing each day's own true historical SafeZone stop, would reopen a genuine 'could decrease later' gap whenever a currently-lower live safezone_stop happens to be the binding term) -- so trailing_stop and protective_stop are independent stop-setting techniques a trader is meant to consider together post-trigger, not one strictly dominating the other.

decisions.decision: Frontend display of the new trailing_stop field (e.g. a PositionsTable/RiskPanel column) is out of scope for this task -- backend computation + API exposure only.
decisions.rationale: The task's own checklist only asks for the backend function, its tests, and wiring into GET /api/portfolio/risk's response contract (regenerating openapi.json/types.ts) -- it doesn't include a frontend checklist item, matching the established split in this same docs/ideas.md ch.53/54 batch (backend-profit-target landed the backend field first; frontend-profit-target-display was a separate, later task that added the UI). decisions.decision: Revisited (per PR #240 review, blocking finding 1): added a nullable `PositionORM.trailing_stop_high_water_mark` column (migration 322370cba3c8), used as a floor in `app.portfolio.risk.ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` (new `persisted_high_water_mark` keyword arg) and written back (`max(existing persisted value, this call's return value)`) by `GET /api/portfolio/risk` at the end of its per-position loop, via a single `db.commit()`. The purely stateless recomputation this task's earlier `decisions` entry chose instead is kept as the base computation (still the primary mechanism, and still correct on its own for a pure price pullback/rally sequence with a fixed cost basis) -- the persisted column is layered on top as a floor, not a full replacement.
decisions.rationale: The reviewer's repro proved the earlier `decisions` entry's own rejection of a persisted column was based on an incomplete threat model: it correctly identified that `POST /api/portfolio/positions`'s same-ticker merge can change `avg_cost_basis`/`entry_date` after a trailing_stop was computed, but concluded the stateless recompute-from-current-cost-basis approach sidestepped that risk entirely, when in fact it has the *identical* defect via a different mechanism -- a HIGHER `avg_cost_basis` after a merge raises `entry_price`/`threshold_profit` in every future recompute, which can un-qualify historical closes that used to cross the trigger and silently DECREASE the reported value (empirically: entered at $100, rallied to $115, ratcheted to ~$101.667; merging in a buy at $200 raises avg_cost_basis to $150 with no further price movement, and a purely stateless recompute alone collapses back down to whatever protective_stop happens to be that day -- observed as low as ~$80.87 in this fix's own regression fixture, or $95.0 in the reviewer's). A pure re-basing/invalidation scheme (recomputing what the ratchet 'should' have been under the new cost basis retroactively) was considered and rejected: it would require reconstructing the OLD cost basis's own ratchet history at merge time (this app doesn't track a history of past avg_cost_basis values, only the current one) to know what floor to carry forward, which is strictly more complex than persisting the one number (the running high-water mark itself) that's actually needed. Persisting only the high-water mark (not the full per-day fold, and not re-deriving anything at merge time) keeps the write minimal: `GET /api/portfolio/risk` becomes this codebase's first side-effecting-write GET route, an accepted, narrow, documented deviation (see this route's own docstring and `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s) now that the alternative -- a value that can silently decrease, contradicting this field's own schema description and docs/Analyse.md's 'Move Your Stop Only in the Direction of Your Trade' -- has been shown to be unacceptable rather than merely inelegant.

decisions.decision: Revisited (per PR #240 review, blocking finding 2): added `trailing_stop` to every frontend `RiskPosition`/`RiskResponse` fixture that previously omitted it (`RiskPanel.test.tsx`, `RiskSummaryCard.test.tsx`, `SellFlaggedPositionsCard.test.tsx`, `tests/mocks/handlers.ts`, and -- for consistency, though its inline `HttpResponse.json` call wasn't type-checked and so wasn't part of the reviewer's 18-error count -- `DashboardPage.test.tsx`), each set equal to that same fixture's own `protective_stop` value (a reasonable 'not yet triggered' placeholder; no test in any of these files asserts on `trailing_stop` itself, since RiskPanel doesn't render it -- see this task's own frontend-out-of-scope `decisions` entry above).

Re-ran `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (0 errors) and `yarn build` (succeeds) after the fix to confirm.

decisions.decision: Round 2 (per PR #240 re-review, both blocking findings): moved the `PositionORM.trailing_stop_high_water_mark` write from `GET /api/portfolio/risk` to `POST /api/portfolio/positions`'s same-ticker-merge branch. `add_position` now takes a `provider: DataProvider = Depends(get_data_provider)` dependency; on a merge, `app.portfolio.risk.trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` (new function: `protective_stop` + `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` composed, degrading to `None` on any fetch/compute failure) is called against the position's OLD, pre-merge `avg_cost_basis`/`entry_date` -- captured into a plain `Position` domain object BEFORE `existing.avg_cost_basis`/`existing.entry_date` are overwritten -- and its result (if not `None`) is written onto `existing.trailing_stop_high_water_mark`. `GET /api/portfolio/risk` no longer mutates `position_row.trailing_stop_high_water_mark` or calls `db.commit()` at all; it only ever reads the column as `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s `persisted_high_water_mark` floor. `docs/Analyse.md` §7 and `docs/architecture/API.md`'s `GET /api/portfolio/risk` section were both corrected to describe this final design (neither still claims the ratchet is 'stateless'/has 'no persisted database state' -- both now explain the two-layer stateless-fold-plus-persisted-floor mechanism and where the write actually lives). Also addressed, since this round already restructured the code: the `backend-trailing-profit-stop-followups` task's 'helper function instead of inline router logic' item is resolved by construction (the write-back logic now lives entirely in `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge`, a two-line call from the router, not inlined comparison logic); its 'concurrency race' item is resolved by the design change itself (the specific race it flagged -- two overlapping GETs racing a lost update -- no longer exists, since GET never writes; the analogous race at the new write site, two overlapping same-ticker merges, shares the exact same read-mutate-commit transaction pattern every other field this same merge branch already mutates -- quantity, avg_cost_basis, entry_notes, strategy -- with no existing locking, so singling out this one field for an atomic `UPDATE ... SET ... = MAX(...)` would be an inconsistent, out-of-scope special case rather than closing a newly-introduced gap). Both followups-task checklist items marked done there with this same rationale.
decisions.rationale: The re-review's blocking finding (design concern, escalated per explicit review-brief instruction) argued `GET /api/portfolio/risk` writing to the database on every call is a genuine, avoidable architectural cost -- it's the first GET route in this codebase with a side effect, violates HTTP GET's safe/idempotent contract (including on an ordinary TanStack Query window-refocus refetch, which `usePortfolioRisk` doesn't disable), and reverses this same codebase's own repeatedly-documented 'annotation happens on read, not on write' convention for POST /api/portfolio/positions and POST /api/watchlist. The reviewer's own suggested alternative -- capture the pre-merge ratchet as a floor at the one write path that can actually invalidate it (the same-ticker merge itself), rather than advancing/persisting it from every subsequent GET -- was adopted as proposed rather than reworked, since (1) it was already fully specified (including the concrete `DataProvider`-dependency addition needed), (2) it keeps every guarantee the previous round's fix established (the ratchet still never decreases across a same-ticker merge that raises `avg_cost_basis` -- verified by keeping the exact same regression test, `test_never_decreases_across_a_same_ticker_merge_that_raises_avg_cost_basis`, passing unchanged end to end through the real POST+GET routes), and (3) it removes rather than merely relocates the side-effecting-GET precedent, which is the more conservative outcome given the reviewer's own explicit uncertainty about whether the alternative's added complexity (a new `DataProvider` dependency + failure-mode handling in the merge handler) was worth it -- not needing a second opinion once the write no longer exists on any GET route at all. A market-data fetch failure at merge time (unknown/delisted ticker, provider down) degrades to leaving any existing floor untouched, matching every other market-data-dependent computation's degrade-gracefully convention in this router; this is a genuinely narrower failure surface than GET's old write (which ran on every poll, not just the relatively rare event of adding to an existing position). Also discovered and fixed along the way: every existing merge test in `tests/integration/test_portfolio_positions.py` used the shared, provider-override-free `client` fixture from `conftest.py`, which meant adding an unconditional `DataProvider` dependency to `add_position` would have made all ~40 of those tests exercise the real, live-network-backed `get_data_provider()` on every merge (only caught because the test suite runtime jumped from ~0.7s to ~21s locally) -- fixed by giving this test module its own local `client`/`_StubProvider` fixture (mirroring the established `test_portfolio_delete_position.py` pattern), restoring near-zero runtime and closing what would otherwise have been a `docs/architecture/Testing.md` 'no test makes a live network call' violation baked into this exact fix. Confirmed still green after this round: full backend suite (1170 passed, 99.95%+ coverage incl. 100% on app/portfolio/risk.py and app/api/routers/portfolio.py), ruff/mypy clean on every touched file, frontend `yarn tsc -b --noEmit`/`yarn build`/`yarn lint`/`vitest` (704 passed) all clean, `backend/openapi.json` + `frontend/src/api/types.ts` regenerated (docstring-only diff, no schema/type shape change), profit-target stale-wording guard clean, all 5 DB migration tests pass.

decisions.rationale: No alternative approach was considered here -- the reviewer's suggested fix was already fully specified, narrow, and mirrored an established pattern used twice already in the same file, so there was no genuine judgment call left to make about *how* to fix it, only whether a 4th automated round was authorized to proceed at all (the orchestrator's own retry-count policy, not a technical ambiguity). Recording this as a `decisions` entry rather than leaving the `questions` entry as the only trace, since CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule asks for the resolution of a `waiting_input` state to itself be recorded (an answered `questions` entry stays in place as history; the answer/resumption is what a fresh `decisions` entry documents).

round_3_comments.summary: RESOLVED from prior round, verified independently: `GET /api/portfolio/risk` is genuinely a pure read again. Traced the full handler body top to bottom -- no `db.commit()`/`db.add()` anywhere in `get_risk` or in any function it calls (`enrich_positions_with_price`, `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`, etc.); the only `db.commit()`/`db.add()` calls left in `portfolio.py` are in unrelated routes (`add_position`, the closed-trades/delete routes). `test_get_risk_never_writes_to_the_database` (mocks `Session.commit` and asserts not-called, plus re-reads the ORM row afterward and confirms `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` is still `None`) passes. Not re-opening this finding.

RESOLVED from prior round, verified independently: the merge-time floor is captured against the OLD, pre-merge position state, in the correct order. `add_position`'s merge branch builds `old_position` from `existing.avg_cost_basis`/`existing.entry_date` (lines 444-450) and calls `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` (line 455) *before* `existing.avg_cost_basis`/`existing.entry_date` are overwritten (lines 461-463) -- confirmed by direct code reading, not just docstring claims.

RESOLVED from prior round, verified independently: the original round-1 bug scenario (rally then a same-ticker merge that raises avg_cost_basis) does not regress under the new design. `test_never_decreases_across_a_same_ticker_merge_that_raises_avg_cost_basis` reproduces the reviewer's exact numbers end to end through the real POST+GET routes and passes. Independently re-reproduced live against a running dev-mode backend (fixture provider, AAPL rallying from an avg_cost_basis of $150 to a trailing_stop of ~$186.62, then merged with a much higher-cost buy) -- `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` correctly persisted the pre-merge floor at each step and the reported `trailing_stop` never decreased across any merge in that walkthrough.

RESOLVED from prior round, verified independently: a market-data fetch failure during a merge degrades correctly. `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` returns `None` (leaving any existing floor untouched) on `daily_ohlcv=None`, a too-short frame, or a `ValueError` from `protective_stop`/`ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` -- covered by `TestTrailingStopFloorBeforeMerge` and `test_merge_data_provider_failure_does_not_block_the_merge`, both passing. The merge itself always succeeds (201) regardless.

RESOLVED from prior round, verified independently: the live-network-call regression in `test_portfolio_positions.py` is genuinely fixed. Every test in that module uses the module's own local `client` fixture backed by `_StubProvider` (never the real `get_data_provider()`), confirmed by direct code reading. Full backend suite reran in ~33s (not the ~21s previously reported as the regression signal, and nowhere near the pre-fix live-network-affected runtime), 1170 passed.

RESOLVED from prior round, verified independently: `docs/Analyse.md` §7 and `docs/architecture/API.md`'s `GET /api/portfolio/risk` section both now accurately describe the two-layer stateless-fold-plus-persisted-floor design and correctly state the write lives at the merge path, not on GET. No remaining 'implemented statelessly, without any persisted database state' claim in either doc.

Blocking (round 3; RESOLVED in round 4, see comments above): `add_position`'s same-ticker-merge branch feeds the raw `daily_ohlcv` fetched from `provider.get_daily_ohlcv(ticker)` straight into `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` without ever calling `app.signals.engine.drop_malformed_daily_bars` first -- unlike every other daily-OHLCV consumer in this same file (`get_portfolio` line 162, `get_risk`'s own filtering before computing `protective_stop`/`ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`). `drop_malformed_daily_bars` exists specifically because a real, observed yfinance condition can leave a bar with NaN open/high/low and only a garbage/partial close in the cached history. Because `trailing_stop_high_water_mark` is persisted as a MAX-floor (`GET /api/portfolio/risk` always returns `max(fresh_candidate, persisted_high_water_mark)`), a single malformed bar present at merge time can lock in a wildly wrong value FOREVER -- no future correct computation can ever bring a MAX-floor back down. Independently reproduced: a 15-day flat-$100 series with one malformed bar (NaN open/high, close=5000 like a real data glitch) three days before the end, avg_cost_basis=100 -- `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge` on the unfiltered frame returns 1730.0, while the correctly-filtered computation (what GET would report for the identical underlying data) returns 97.0. That 1730.0 would be permanently persisted and reported by every future `GET /api/portfolio/risk` call for this position regardless of real subsequent price action. No test in `TestAddPositionCapturesTrailingStopFloorAtMerge` exercises a malformed frame, so this gap is untested. Fix: filter `daily_ohlcv` through `drop_malformed_daily_bars` (mirroring `get_risk`'s own `require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=False` call) before passing it to `trailing_stop_floor_before_merge`, inside `add_position`'s merge branch.
